mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 3.5% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns do not show a significant positive trend following RSAFS increases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) above 2% YoY signals a strong supply-side economy, which can lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not lead to higher corporate earnings within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% YoY, the real interest rate is high, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced investment and consumption.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the described conditions do not lead to reduced investment and consumption within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strong labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the described labor market conditions do not lead to tighter monetary policy within the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which can lead to negative spillover effects on the broader economy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST < 1 million units does not lead to negative spillover effects on the broader economy within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is growing at a rate above 3% YoY and Real GDP (GDPC1) is growing at a rate below 2% YoY, it indicates a supply-side driven economy with potential inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the described conditions do not lead to inflationary pressures within the next 3 months.
